terms.title: Terms of Use of the “Home Under Control” app
intro: Rights holder and developer: Tagirov Tagir. Contact: tagir.tagirov.987@gmail.com
This is a translation. If it differs from the Russian original, the Russian original prevails.

sections.title: 1. Accepting the terms
sections.text: On first launch the app shows these terms and asks you to accept them; without that its sections are unavailable. If you don’t agree with the terms, don’t use the app and uninstall it. Your consent is stored on your device together with the date and the terms version number and is not sent anywhere.

sections.title: 2. What the app is
sections.text:
“Home Under Control” is a personal record-keeping tool: household deadlines, recurring payments, expenses and meter readings. The app stores information you entered yourself, counts days and amounts and creates reminders on your device.

The app is not connected to banks, payment systems, service providers, insurance companies or government bodies, receives no information from them and makes no payments. The only thing the app receives from the internet is reference exchange rates (section 4).

sections.title: 3. This is not advice
sections.text:
The app gives no legal, immigration, financial, tax, investment or medical advice and no advice on product safety.

• The permitted length of stay and the validity of a visa, insurance, lease or other documents are determined by the documents themselves and by law. The app doesn’t know these rules and counts days only from the date you entered.
• The “time since” counter says nothing about whether a product, medicine or consumable is still fit for use.

Make decisions with legal or financial consequences for you based on the original documents and, if needed, with a qualified specialist.

sections.title: 4. Calculations
sections.text:
Amounts and calculations in the app are for reference only.

• The meter cost estimate uses the tariff or tiers you entered yourself. Tiers apply to the usage between two consecutive readings; taxes, fees and recalculations are not counted separately. The provider’s bill may differ.
• Expense totals include only the records you entered.
• The combined total of expenses in different currencies is an approximate estimate. All expenses of the selected period are converted at the last saved reference rate, not at the rate on the day of each purchase and not at the rate of your bank or exchange office. The amounts of the records themselves don’t change.
• The app gets rates from third-party services (Frankfurter, or ExchangeRate-API when it’s unavailable). They don’t guarantee the accuracy or availability of rates; a rate may be out of date. The rate date and the time of the last check are shown next to the total. If there is no rate for some currency, no combined total is shown — amounts are given per currency.

sections.title: 5. Reminders
sections.text: Notifications are created by the app and shown by the operating system. It may delay or not show a notification — for example, in battery saver, Do Not Disturb, after the app is force-stopped, after a time zone change or after a system update. Don’t rely on the app as your only reminder of a deadline or payment that matters to you.

sections.title: 6. Your data
sections.text:
Data is stored only on your device. The developer has no access to it and can’t restore it.

You are responsible for keeping your data safe: for locking your device and for backups. Data will be lost if the device is lost, broken or reset, the app is uninstalled or the encryption key is lost, unless you have a saved backup. A password-protected backup can’t be opened without the password.

The exchange-rate request contains none of your records: only currency codes are sent. How the app handles data, permissions and the internet is described in the privacy policy.

sections.title: 7. Voice input
sections.text: Speech is turned into text by your device’s recognition service. If the language model isn’t installed on the device, audio is processed by Google or Apple under their own terms. Recognition results may be inaccurate: check the record before saving.

sections.title: 8. Acceptable use
sections.text: The app is intended for personal use. You may not decompile or modify the app, circumvent its technical restrictions, distribute copies of it or use its name and design without the rights holder’s written permission — except where such a right is expressly granted by law.

sections.title: 9. Intellectual property
sections.text: The app, its code, design and name belong to the rights holder. Third-party components belong to their authors and are used under their licenses; the list and license texts are available in the app on the “About” screen.

sections.title: 10. No warranty
sections.text: The app is provided “as is” and “as available”. The developer doesn’t guarantee that it will work without errors or interruptions, that calculations will be accurate or that reminders will arrive on time.

sections.title: 11. Limitation of liability
sections.text:
To the extent permitted by applicable law, the developer is not liable for indirect and incidental losses, lost profits and data loss arising from using the app or being unable to use it — including missed deadlines and payments, fines, penalties and costs related to a calculation error or a reminder that didn’t work. The developer’s total liability is limited to the amount you paid for the app in the last twelve months.

These terms don’t limit consumer rights and liability that can’t be limited under the law of your country.

sections.title: 12. Paid features
sections.text: The app is currently free. If paid features appear, purchases will be made through the app store under its rules, including refund rules; the terms of paid features will be published before they appear.

sections.title: 13. Changes
sections.text: The app and these terms may change. A new version of the terms is published at the same link with a new date. If the terms change significantly — for example, data transfer or paid features appear — the app will show the new version and ask you to accept it again. Clarifying the wording doesn’t require new consent.

sections.title: 14. Contacts
sections.text: Questions about the terms: tagir.tagirov.987@gmail.com.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy of the “Home Under Control” app
intro: This is a translation. If it differs from the Russian original, the Russian original prevails.

sections.title: In short
sections.text:
The app doesn’t collect your data. Everything you enter is stored only on your device. The app has no servers, accounts, ads or analytics.

The app goes online for one purpose only — to get exchange rates. That request contains none of your records: only currency codes.

sections.title: What data you enter
Permissions
sections.text:
• Camera and photos — to take or choose a photo of a meter. The photo is shown on screen so it’s easy to copy the reading; the app doesn’t save it or send it anywhere.
• Microphone and speech recognition — to add an expense by voice. Speech is turned into text by your phone’s system service. If the Russian language model is installed on the device, audio doesn’t leave the device. If not, audio is processed by Google (on Android) or Apple (on iPhone) speech recognition under their own rules. The app receives only text and doesn’t save the recording. Before first use the app shows this explanation and asks for consent; you can withdraw it in settings.
• Notifications — to remind you of deadlines and payments and, if you turned on the evening reminder, once a day — when no expense was added that day — to suggest adding your spending. Notifications are created on the device, without a server. By default they contain no names or amounts; the evening reminder never contains them.
• Biometrics — to open the app if you turned on the lock. The check is done by the system; the app never receives your fingerprint or face image.

Each permission is requested when you use the corresponding feature. Refusing doesn’t stop you from entering data manually.

sections.title: Internet access
sections.text:
The app goes online only for exchange rates — to show the combined total of expenses in the currency you chose.

• When. When you open the app, if a week has passed since the last successful check or the saved rate is older than a week, and when you tap “Update rate”. There are no requests in the background while the app is closed. Automatic checks can be turned off in settings.
• Where. The Frankfurter service (api.frankfurter.dev); if it’s unavailable — ExchangeRate-API (open.er-api.com). The app has no access keys or accounts with these services.
• What is sent. Only the app’s currency codes (VND, RUB, USD, EUR) in the request address — the same for all users. Your expenses, amounts, notes, names and any other records are not sent.
• What the service may see. The device’s IP address, the time of the request and technical details of the connection — like any website you open. How the services handle this information is governed by their own rules: frankfurter.dev and exchangerate-api.com. The app developer doesn’t receive this information.
• What stays on the device. The rates received, the date of those rates and the time of the last check. Without internet the app works as usual and uses the last saved rate.

sections.title: Sharing with third parties
sections.text: The app doesn’t share your data with third parties and doesn’t sell it. The exchange-rate request contains none of your records.

sections.title: Backups
sections.text:
You can save a copy of your data to a file. Where to send the file is up to you; from then on its safety depends on the place you chose. A backup can be protected with a password. A forgotten password can’t be recovered. Saved exchange rates, the chosen appearance and language, evening reminder settings and “Didn’t spend today” marks are not included in the backup: they belong to this device.

Android system backup is turned off for the app. On iPhone the database file may end up in your iCloud or computer backup if such backups are on; it stays encrypted, and the key isn’t included in the backup.

sections.title: Deleting data
sections.text: App settings have “Delete all data”: records and settings are erased from the device permanently. Uninstalling the app also deletes all its data. The app can’t delete backup files you saved earlier — delete them wherever they are.

sections.title: Children
sections.text: The app isn’t intended for children under 13 and doesn’t knowingly collect their data — just as it doesn’t collect the data of any other users.

sections.title: Changes
sections.text: If the policy changes, the new version will appear at this same link with a new date. The app will tell you about significant changes when it updates.
